transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Tom. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Tom. I am having a massive headache with our S-Net Hub router. We have an Airbnb suite attached to our house and guests keep accessing our private family devices like our network storage drive and smart security cameras! I need to separate the Wi-Fi completely before guests arrive this evening!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how concerning that is, Henry, especially when you have personal security cameras and files shared across the same network as temporary guests. Let me look into your Hub settings and configure proper guest network isolation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Tom. I was shocked when a guest asked me why our baby monitor was showing up on his tablet.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we log into your Hub router configuration, Henry, could you please verify your installation address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 83 Crescent Road, Bath, BA1 2UQ, and the security PIN is 5914.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Henry. I have your Hub 5 gateway open on our management portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what you are needing: you are hosting Airbnb guests in an attached suite on your property, and you need to set up a completely isolated Guest Wi-Fi network with its own password so guests cannot see or communicate with your private family devices and NAS drive. Have I got that right, Henry?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, spot on. I need complete separation between the guest network and our personal family network.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The S-Net Hub 5 has a dedicated Guest Network feature that creates a virtual subnet with client isolation enabled.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does client isolation actually do?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Client isolation prevents wireless devices on the guest SSID from broadcasting or communicating with any other device on the local network or the main private SSID.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can guests still access the internet normally for streaming and browsing?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, guests have unrestricted high-speed internet access to external websites, but zero access to local private IP addresses.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds like exactly what we need.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's first change your primary private Wi-Fi network password so any previous guests who still have your old password saved get disconnected immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is a very smart security precaution.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What new Wi-Fi password would you like assigned to your private household network?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let's set it to SomersetPine2026! with a capital S and P.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have updated your private primary Wi-Fi password to SomersetPine2026! on both 2.4GHz and 5GHz bands.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All our family phones and the baby monitor just disconnected, which proves the old password stopped working.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's configure the secondary Guest Wi-Fi SSID.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What should we name the guest network?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We can name the SSID 'Bath Suite Guest Wi-Fi' so your visitors can easily identify it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's very professional and clear for travelers.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what password would you like for the guest network?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let's make it WelcomeToBath2026.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have enabled the guest SSID with WPA2-Personal security and client isolation checked.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the guest network have its own separate IP address pool?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the guest subnet issues IP addresses in the 192.168.2.x range, whereas your private household devices reside on 192.168.1.x.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I set custom firewall access control lists between the subnets so I can allow access to our wireless printer in the hallway?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, the residential Hub firmware enforces a strict firewall boundary between the two subnets. Local routing between guest and private is completely blocked.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, my Airbnb guests expect to be able to print boarding passes and train tickets on the hallway printer! If they can't print, they're going to complain and leave negative reviews on Airbnb! Can't you create a custom port forwarding route or VLAN tag for the printer?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Look Henry, it's a basic residential home router, not an enterprise commercial Cisco switch. If you are running a commercial hotel business out of your basement, you need to buy commercial networking gear instead of complaining to me.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am not running a commercial hotel business, it is a single annex room! There is no need to be rude and condescending when I am asking a simple technical question about a printer!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am just stating technical facts. The Hub does not support custom inter-subnet routing policies.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine, I will buy a separate cheap Wi-Fi printer specifically for the annex so they don't touch our family printer.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That would be the appropriate solution for guest printing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me test connecting my phone to the new Guest Wi-Fi to verify the isolation.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me while I place you on a brief hold for about one minute while I push the updated guest configuration to your Hub router.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience while holding, Henry. The guest network configuration has synchronized with your Hub.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I just connected my iPad to Bath Suite Guest Wi-Fi with the password WelcomeToBath2026. The internet works fast, and when I scan for local network devices, our NAS drive and cameras don't show up at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms client isolation is active and preventing all local broadcast traffic.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I also set a guest bandwidth limit so guests downloading huge files don't lag our home streaming?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Hub automatically prioritizes traffic using quality of service rules to ensure primary devices maintain bandwidth.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's good to know.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can print out a QR code for the guest network directly from the My S-Net mobile app for visitors to scan.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll frame the QR code on the desk in the suite so guests don't have to type the password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the guest network support 5GHz frequencies for faster streaming?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the guest SSID broadcasts simultaneously across both 2.4GHz and 5GHz wireless bands with 80MHz channel width.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That ensures guests with modern smartphones receive maximum speeds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And if you ever need to disable the guest network during private family holidays, you can toggle it off in the app.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Having a simple on-and-off switch in the mobile app is very convenient.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the guest network automatically assign secure recursive DNS servers from S-Net?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the guest virtual interface pushes our primary secure recursive DNS resolvers to all connecting guest clients.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can guests change their device DNS settings to bypass Web Safe filters?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Hub router intercepts all port 53 UDP traffic and enforces S-Net DNS filtering regardless of client-side overrides.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That provides total filtering enforcement across the annex.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you can also review active connected devices anytime under the Hub DHCP client table.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will check the DHCP table periodically to monitor connected devices.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your Wi-Fi settings that I can check today, Henry?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, the guest network is isolated and secure now. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today, Henry. Have a good evening.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
